summary.headline: TARIL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 66% YoY to INR709 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 16.1%, with order book at INR7,237 crore (+32% YoY).
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR709 crore (+66% YoY, +27% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR114 crore (+203% YoY), with margin at 16.1% versus 8.8% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher utilisation and operating leverage. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,268 crore (+35% YoY) and EBITDA INR185 crore (14.6% margin). Order inflow in Q2 was INR1,169 crore (+97% YoY off a low base), and the unexecuted order book stood at INR7,237 crore, executable over 18-24 months. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 9-10% PAT margin, while working-capital days (about 154) remain the key drag on cash flow.

+47% YoY; margin 14.6% vs 13.4% in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR575 crore (LT ~INR125 crore, ST ~INR449 crore)

segments.name: Power transformers / high voltage
segments.commentary: About 55-60% of the order book is 400 kV and above. Management said about 56% of power transformer execution in Q2 was in this class. Q2 margin gains were attributed to higher utilisation at the Moraiya plant.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 8% of Q2 revenue and about 15% of the order book. Export inquiries are about 20% of the INR21,000 crore inquiry pipeline.

segments.name: Backward integration (CTC, bushings, tanks, pressboard)
segments.commentary: CTC plant to be commissioned around Diwali, with commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27; about 60% of its 3,000 MTPA capacity is captive. Management expects 200-300 bps margin expansion once integration is complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: 25% revenue growth (target 25% and beyond) with 9-10% PAT margin, per management's reply to analyst questions.
Working capital cycle to fall below 120 days, targeted from end of FY27, with 110-120 days in the year; this is expected to make free cash flow positive.
Changodar expansion (about 35,000 MVA total capacity, incremental capex about INR150 crore) to start commercial production around Diwali; Moraiya EHV capacity to follow.
Management targets about USD1 billion revenue, expected late FY29 or early 2030, including bushings, pressboard, CRGO, CTC, and tank sales; no additional capex is planned.
HVDC converter transformer capability expected within 18 months; BESS transformer orders expected in the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Changodar: total capacity to reach about 35,000 MVA (incremental about 25,000 MVA on 12,000 MVA existing) for distribution, IDT, renewable transformers, and small power and LV transformers up to 132 kV, plus large power transformers up to 220 kV; capex about INR150 crore; commercial production around Diwali.
Moraiya: planned EHV transformer capacity of about 22,000 MVA after Changodar is complete; insulation/pressboard plant is adding about 30% manufacturing capacity at Moraiya once functional.
CTC plant (3,000 MTPA): machinery being installed; commissioning before Diwali, trial runs in Nov-Dec, commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27, external sales from Q1 FY28.
Q2 FY27 production was about 9,500 MVA. Management's ideal utilisation is about 90%, targeted in FY28 or FY29.
HVDC: repair of a PGCIL transformer takes about 4-5 months, then 6-7 months of operation before qualification; re-engineering is under way.
demand_pricing: Order inflow: NPCIL Kaiga Units 5 and 6 generator transformers (first nuclear order, 400 kV+, competed with Crompton and others; repeatable). Megha Engineering order (35-month execution). Damodar Valley Corporation order (500 MVA and 200 MVA; 15-28 months). GETCO order (80 and 125 MVAr reactors, 500 MVA auto-transformers; 24-30 months). APTRANSCO LOI. PGCIL order of about INR1,000 crore (24-28 months; manufacturing from December FY28).
Inquiries under negotiation are INR21,000 crore, about 80% domestic and 20% export, split equally between government and private customers.

Realisation is about INR7 lakh per MVA on average. Price variation clauses are billed every quarter. Management attributed about 7-8% of revenue growth to price variation, with no list price increase in Q2.
Competition: management sees no major price war, since competitors also hold large order books. Kanohar competes in 132 kV and 220 kV.

Raw materials (transoil, CRGO, copper) remain high-priced; Middle East disruption has not hit imports materially, but timely availability of some critical raw materials is an issue. Inventory is sufficient until Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Details of Kaiga and Megha orders; is Kaiga repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaiga was competed against Crompton and others for generator transformers at 400 kV+; management expects repeat NPCIL orders. Greenfield nuclear transformer content is about 15-18% of the transformer cost.

qa_highlights.question: Mix of order book by voltage class?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55-60% of the order book is 400 kV and above; about 56% of Q2 power transformer execution was in this class.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to cut working-capital days from end-FY27, targeting below 120 days and 110-120 days this year, which should lead to positive cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation per MVA and capex on Changodar?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation about INR7 lakh per MVA; Changodar capex about INR150 crore for about 35,000 MVA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance looks conservative given H2 run rate; can FY27 revenue reach INR3,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it maintains the INR3,200 crore FY27 revenue target and the 9-10% PAT margin. It needs to execute about INR900 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a path to USD1 billion revenue and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects USD1 billion by late FY29 or early FY30 from transformers plus bushings, pressboard, CRGO, CTC, and tank sales. It said no additional capex is needed.

risks_watch: Working-capital intensity: inventory about INR654 crore and receivables about INR1,053 crore against INR1,268 crore H1 revenue. Operating cash flow conversion is weak relative to PAT.
Commissioning timelines for Changodar (around Diwali) and CTC (Q3 FY27, commercial from Q4) could slip; the CTC timeline was questioned against earlier guidance of Q2 FY27.
Raw material price volatility and supply of critical inputs amid Middle East disruption; part of the order book has price variation clauses, but the rest does not.
Retention money of about INR200 crore (5-10% of order value) is tied up on the balance sheet.
HVDC and converter transformer qualification is roughly 1.5 years away; BESS orders are not yet in hand.
Pricing: about 7-8% of revenue growth came from price variation; underlying realisation trends need to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order visibility, and on margins and the expansion timeline. Management was less precise on cash-flow timing, CTC commissioning dates (which shifted from Q2 to Q3 FY27), and HVDC qualification.
key_quotes: As of 30th September 2026, our unexecuted order book stood at 7,237 crore, up by 32% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility over the medium term.
EBITDA margin improved to 16.1% compared to 8.8% in Q2FY26 and 13.3% in Q1 FY27.
Following our Q2 performance, we remain confident of achieving FY27 guidance and continue to remain on track with our growth plans for the full year.
So, we are pretty much sure that we'll reach USD1 billion.

growth.why: Management held FY27 guidance of 25%+ revenue growth and ~16% EBITDA margin; backing is a INR7,237 crore order book (+32% YoY) and Changodar capacity (~INR150 crore capex, commercial production around Diwali), but no explicit quarter-by-quarter bridge was given and ~7-8% of growth came from price variation, so backing is partial.
